newsitem.title: UK: No sign of pound's strength reversing - CBI's Buxton.
newsitem.headline: No sign of pound's strength reversing - CBI's Buxton.

text.p: Andrew Buxton, chairman of the Confederation of British Industry's economic affairs committee, said on Monday there was no sign of the pound's strength reversing.
"One can't see the strength of the pound reversing," he told reporters at the CBI's annual conference. "The pressure on (interest) rates in Europe is largely down and here it is up."
Buxton said the pound's rally was a concern for exporters, but said there was no set rate for sterling at which alarm bells would start ringing louder.
The pound has appreciated around nine percent on a trade- weighted basis in the past three months.
Buxton said the recent quarter-point interest rate rise was a surprise, and came a little too soon for the CBI's liking, but was small enough in itself to make only a marginal difference.
But he did not wish to see more base rate rises in the near future, which could push the pound higher still.
"We would be concerned at seeing future rate rises unless there is clear evidence of inflationary effects," Buxton said. "We can't see them developing yet."
